question.leadin: Identify these politicians who were powerful during the 1990's.
question.text: This Georgia Republican served as Speaker of the House from 1995 to 1999 and was a co-writer of the Contract with America.
question.clue: This former Speaker of the House from Georgia won the South Carolina primary. During the campaign, he proposed a moon colony that could petition to become a U.S. state.

swap.text: In a tweet, this South Carolina senator stated that "any policy proposal which drives up costs of Corona, tequila, or margaritas is a big-time bad idea" in response to a 20% income tax with Mexico to pay the wall.
swap.clue: This Senator, who is widely rumored to be gay, has remained low in the polls but was widely regarded as the winner of the September 16th "kid's table" debate.

question.text: The first Jewish woman to serve on the Supreme Court, she served for 13 years on the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit before being nominated by Bill Clinton in 1993.
question.clue: This co-founder of the ACLU's Women's Rights Project struck down VMI's male-only admission policy as part of her longtime advocacy for women's rights.

swap.leadin: In 2010, he resigned as the U.S. Commander in Afghanistan in response to fallout from an interview with Rolling Stone magazine.

question.leadin: This politician faced criticism from Catholics when he boycotted New York City's annual St. Patrick's Day parade, citing the organizers' exclusion of LGBT groups.
question.text: Name this man who won the November 2013 mayoral election, handily defeating Republican Joe Lhota.
question.clue: This politician once fatally dropped a rodent named Chuck during a Groundhog Day ceremony, and successfully established a universal free pre-K program in his city.

question.leadin: In order to calculate this metric for an election, net wasted votes are divided by the total number of votes cast.
question.text: Name this objective computer-implemented metric devised by law professor Nicholas Stephanopoulos and political scientist Eric McGhee to nullify the ability to gerrymander in a partisan fashion.
question.clue: One element of Gill lacking in previous gerrymandering cases is the use of this metric, which quantifies the number of "wasted votes" for each party. This metric was developed by Stephanopoulos and McGhee at UChicago.
